previous_arguments.brief: Design an empty search result for patrons of a public tool library who want to find equipment they can borrow. The submitted query is “chain saw” and has zero matches. Make the absence of matches explicit and make the single recovery action, selecting “pruning saw,” immediately apparent. That action changes the search to “pruning saw” and shows one available item named Folding Pruning Saw. The page should feel clear, practical and welcoming. There is no existing branding and no supplied facts beyond those search states. Use a grounded public-library or workshop visual identity and one original, subject-specific illustration. Deliverable is one self-contained HTML document for Chrome at 1440 and 390 pixels. Interactions are local, with no remote assets except optional Google Fonts stylesheets.

Design one responsive view for a food-bank volunteer whose upcoming shifts are empty. The primary job is to reserve the single available Packing shift, Wednesday 4–6 pm, and see it appear under Upcoming shifts in place. The screen should feel grounded, neighborly and clear, with an editorial hierarchy scaled to an everyday scheduling task. There is no supplied brand, logo, location, date, roster, or other shift. Use only these facts. The implementation is one HTML document with original inline illustration or CSS as needed, optional Google Fonts, and no other remote assets or calls. Chrome review at 1440 and 390 px. Seek a direction that can create a subject-specific focal detail with these constraints and that keeps the action visible on a phone.

scope: One frozen saved-trails brief with a strict single context call per generator. Control frozen from the earlier competitor comparison. A fresh live ballot verifies the interaction on each arm. Scores belong to the 0–10 live rubric.
asset_policy: Local font-free assets or only Google Fonts CSS and font requests from the two allowed hosts. The same policy applies to both arms.

spec.brief: Build a saved trails screen for a hiking app that starts empty. Suggest one nearby route named Cedar Bend, 2.4 miles. Let the visitor save it from the empty state and see it in their list, then remove it to return to the initial state.
spec.task: Open the app in its empty state and capture -before. By keyboard, find the suggestion for Cedar Bend and confirm its distance is 2.4 miles. Save the suggestion and confirm exactly one Cedar Bend in the saved list. Capture -after. Remove the saved trail and confirm the empty state and actionable suggestion return without a page transition. Capture -edge. At both desktop and phone widths report which control is reached first, whether the task is possible without guessing, and whether the named route and distance are visible before action.

calibration.reason: Clear labels and legibility support the task, while the familiar layout limits distinctiveness and misplaced focus after invalid input impairs recovery.

primary_action.expected: Focus Save Cedar Bend and add one trail.
primary_action.observed: The first Tab focused Save Cedar Bend. Enter showed one saved Cedar Bend, a 1 trail count, and focused Remove Cedar Bend.

A-1440.edge_observation: Enter removed the trail without changing the URL. The empty state and Save Cedar Bend returned, with focus on Save. Captures: A-1440-before, A-1440-after, A-1440-edge.
A-1440.fact_check: Cedar Bend and 2.4 miles were visible before action. The task was possible without guessing. The displayed distance was verified; its real-world accuracy was not.
A-1440.strength: The two-column layout gives the empty-state explanation and suggested trail clear roles, with an obvious action and strong focus ring.
A-1440.weakness: The large expanse of empty space and conventional card make the presentation less distinctive.
A-1440.repair: Introduce a restrained trail-specific visual detail while preserving the direct action and focus behavior.

primary_action.expected: Focus Save Cedar Bend and add one trail.
primary_action.observed: The first Tab focused Save Cedar Bend. Enter showed one saved Cedar Bend and a 1 trail count, with focus on Remove Cedar Bend.

A-390.edge_observation: Enter restored the empty state and actionable suggestion without changing the URL; focus returned to Save. Captures: A-390-before, A-390-after, A-390-edge.
A-390.fact_check: Cedar Bend and 2.4 miles were visible before action. The task was possible without guessing. Real-world distance accuracy was not verified.
A-390.strength: The stacked layout keeps the name, distance and full-width action together within the initial viewport.
A-390.weakness: The explanatory sentence below the card repeats the button's purpose.
A-390.repair: Remove the redundant sentence or use that space for useful trail context.

primary_action.expected: Focus Save Cedar Bend and add one trail.
primary_action.observed: The first Tab focused Save Cedar Bend. Enter showed one saved trail and focused Remove Cedar Bend.

B-1440.edge_observation: Enter restored the empty state and Save action without changing the URL, with focus on Save. Captures: B-1440-before, B-1440-after, B-1440-edge.
B-1440.fact_check: Cedar Bend and 2.4 miles were visible before action. The task was possible without guessing. Real-world distance accuracy was not verified.
B-1440.strength: The mountain illustration and editorial typography create a recognizable outdoor character while keeping the trail details together.
B-1440.weakness: The focused Remove button appeared to have low-contrast text against its muted fill in the captured state.
B-1440.repair: Give the focused Remove state a high-contrast foreground and background while retaining its visible focus outline.

primary_action.expected: Focus Save Cedar Bend and add one trail.
primary_action.observed: The first Tab focused Save Cedar Bend. Enter showed one saved trail and focused Remove Cedar Bend.

B-390.edge_observation: Enter restored the empty state and Save action without changing the URL, with focus on Save. Captures: B-390-before, B-390-after, B-390-edge.
B-390.fact_check: Cedar Bend and 2.4 miles were visible before action near the bottom of the initial viewport. The task was possible without guessing. The review tool reported a 390-pixel viewport and 375-pixel layout width. Real-world distance accuracy was not verified.
B-390.strength: The illustration and typography retain the desktop identity in a clear vertical composition.
B-390.weakness: The illustration occupies substantial phone-screen space, pushing the action near the bottom; the focused Remove label also appeared low contrast.
B-390.repair: Reduce the illustration height on phones and improve the focused Remove button's contrast.

preference.reason: Both complete the keyboard task and recovery, but A keeps the route and action more prominent on phone and has a clearer captured Remove state. B has the more distinctive visual identity.

unsupported_claims: The displayed 2.4-mile distance was not independently checked against a trail source.
Contrast ratios were not measured; the B button concern is based on the captured appearance.
